items.title: Heat exchanger moved heat from cold to hot
items.failed: GEMINI's HeatExchanger took the absolute temperature difference and applied it with fixed signs, so heat flowed from cold to hot when the secondary inlet was the hotter stream. Primary 20 °C and secondary 60 °C (150/150 m³/h, UA 250 kW/K) came out at −3.05 °C and 83.05 °C.
items.fix: Patch 01 uses the signed temperature difference for the maximum duty (checked: 20 → 43.05 °C and 60 → 36.95 °C).

items.title: Heat pump solver returned a spurious root
items.failed: HeatpumpBasic minimised a sum of residuals with Nelder-Mead, with no bounds and no check of convergence. In a cascade it gave COP 1.09, 311 °C, 24.8 MW of heat and 22.6 MW of power against the correct COP 6.15, 72.2 °C, 2.52 MW and 0.41 MW, and it divided by zero when Ts_in equalled Th_out_target.
items.found: Bug hunt 27 Oct: repro scripts 02b_heatpump_grid.py and 13_heatpump_cascade.py
items.fix: Patch 04 uses the closed form in Carnot mode and a bracketed root (brentq) for the source-limited and Lorenz cases; errors were 1e-13 on the full grid, with no exceptions.

items.title: Injection well friction had the wrong sign
items.failed: The simulator passed the injector's flow as +Q with direction 'down', so tubing friction was added instead of subtracted: bottomhole pressure 267.09 bar against 263.41 bar. On a challenge design the released code gives 0.007 MW of injection pump power against 0.263 MW (together with the roughness default, F10).
items.fix: Patch 02 passes the injector's flow as −Q to the pressure-drop model.

items.title: Producer flow solve could return a non-physical root
items.failed: GEMINI's nodal solve searches 0.01–700 m³/h on an extrapolated ESP curve and clamps the pump intake at 0 bar. In the repro it had roots at 213.6, 376.8 and 598.5 m³/h and returned 598.6 m³/h with an ESP head of 3312 bar and 3230 % efficiency, with no warning.
items.fix: Not patched. Dioscuri calls GEMINI's flow solve with a bracket of 0.6 to 1.4 times the design flow (src/gemini_agent/tools/gemini.py, next to FLOW_BRACKET_M3H), which keeps the physical root.

items.title: ESP affinity law applied without scaling the flow
items.failed: The ESP model used (f/60)²·H60(Q) and (f/60)³·P60(Q) instead of evaluating the 60 Hz curves at Q·60/f. Efficiency reached 105.8 % at 40 Hz, and ESP power was off by −20 % at 40 Hz, −15 % at 45 Hz and +8 % at 70 Hz.
items.fix: Patch 05 evaluates the 60 Hz curves at Q·60/f; efficiency is then 68.2 % at 40, 50, 60 and 70 Hz on affinity-similar points.

items.title: Recycle loops were not converged
items.failed: GEMINI's solver makes one sequential sweep per time step, with no iteration or residual check. A closed secondary loop (exchanger, 15 K consumer, exchanger) gave 3.383 MW after one run against 2.756 MW converged (+23 %), and nothing said so.
items.fix: Not patched. Dioscuri's GEMINI brine loop gives the heat network's return temperature to the heat exchanger as a boundary input (src/gemini_agent/tools/gemini.py, plant_project), so it has no recycle loop.

items.title: Compressor power was low by a factor k
items.failed: The compressor used n·m·R·T1/(k−1)·(…) instead of n·m·k/(k−1)·R·T1·(…). It gave 355.0 kW against 461.4 kW by hand: −23 % at k = 1.3 and −29 % at k = 1.4.
items.fix: Patch 06 adds the missing factor k; the result matches the hand calculation for 1, 2 and 3 stages.

items.title: Borehole heat exchanger stepped twice per solver step
items.failed: On GEMINI's geoloop branch the BHE's calculate_output also updated its state and re-ran its whole history. Five solver steps made 10 history entries, and 200 hourly steps took 218 s, so a yearly run was infeasible.
items.fix: Not patched. The BHE model is on GEMINI's geoloop branch, and no Dioscuri design uses a borehole heat exchanger.

items.title: Two-phase well pressure drop used the wrong gas velocity
items.failed: The two-phase path computed the superficial gas velocity from gmf instead of the gas mass flow, with a constant gas density at standard conditions. With GMF = 1e-4 the wellhead pressure jumped from 4.5 to 26 bar.
items.found: Bug hunt 27 Oct: repro script 07_misc_components.py (last block)
items.fix: Patch 07 uses the gas mass flow for the superficial gas velocity; the gas PVT is still constant, and Dioscuri's well configs leave GMF at its default of 0.

items.title: Default well roughness was 10 mm, documented as mm
items.failed: The well-flow default roughness was 0.01 m (10 mm), while the code comment and docs say the unit is mm. Friction was 4.3–5.4 times that of steel at 4.5e-5 m, and the example doublet ran at 129 m³/h instead of 203 m³/h.
items.found: Bug hunt 27 Oct: repro script 04_wells.py (blocks C, D and D2)
items.fix: Patch 03 sets the default roughness to 4.5e-5 m (0.045 mm, steel), and patch 07 corrects the unit comment.

items.title: Heat pump reported no CO2
items.failed: HeatpumpBasic reported zero CO2 because its electricity was not counted. For the challenge design 1D-HP-EC@3000 the released code gives 0 kg/h of heat pump CO2 against 86 kg/h.
items.found: Running Dioscuri's designs on GEMINI's solver, 29 Oct
items.fix: Patch 08 counts the CO2 of the heat pump's electricity, with an optional electricity_emission_factor.

items.title: Simulator registry had no heat pump
items.failed: GEMINI's component registry had no heat pump, so a simulator project could not use one.
items.found: Running Dioscuri's designs on GEMINI's solver, 29 Oct
items.fix: Patch 09 registers HeatpumpBasic as 'heatpump'.

items.title: Heat pump Carnot COP taken at the source inlet
items.failed: The Carnot COP used the source's inlet temperature. With brine cooled from 53 to 30 °C, that gave a COP above the physical Carnot limit.
items.found: Running Dioscuri's designs on GEMINI's solver, 29 Oct
items.fix: Patch 10 (applied after 04) takes the Carnot COP at the source outlet, where the evaporator runs, and both modes solve the source balance.

items.title: Well model used water, not the brine
items.failed: The well model's fluid was water at standard conditions, hard-coded in _build_dpdt, not the challenge brine (1,030 kg/m³, 0.40 mPa·s). With the 10 mm roughness (F10) the released code gives an ESP head of 41.7 bar at 300 m³/h against 31.1 bar (+34 %).
items.found: Building the challenge doublet on GEMINI's well model, 30 Oct
items.fix: Patch 11 lets a well config pass the fluid (RHOL, VISL, CPL), and Dioscuri passes the brine; without it, behaviour is unchanged.

items.title: A hard cap relaxed by asking still showed as passed
items.failed: Asked to run 365 days, the design accepted it, and the 330-day check renamed itself 'At most 365 days per doublet' and passed.
items.fix: A relaxed cap is still checked against the challenge's 330 days, and the check and the inputs card say what was asked.

items.title: Dioscuri's GEMINI brine loop went below vacuum
items.failed: The brine loop Dioscuri drew as a GEMINI project went to negative pressure after the filters (−1.62 and −2.24 bar; −5.9 bar at the injection pump suction with a shared train), and the run still reported ok.
items.fix: The treatment train is sized for a 1 bar drop at its flow and the duty ESP runs at 70 %, so GEMINI's pumps equal the plant model's (0.391 MW ESP, 0.221 MW injection at 300 m³/h); a run warns on any pressure below 1 bar.

items.title: GEMINI's example ESP had negative head at the design flow
items.failed: GEMINI's example ESP is sized for about 150 m³/h and gave a negative head at the design's 300 m³/h, so the GEMINI tab's ESP power (24 kW) was meaningless.
items.fix: The GEMINI view scales the same pump family to each producer's duty (the design flow at 60 % of run-out, stages for the head needed at 55 Hz).

items.title: One unit out was never checked
items.failed: No design was checked with one unit out: with either doublet out the design was 7.17 MW short on 70 days, and the outage answer said the town stays warm.
items.found: Review panel 31 Oct (operator, geothermal specialist, district energy engineer)
items.fix: Every design gets each one-unit-out case and the peak-day spare (dioscuri_plant.firm), and the answer model gets them as conclusions.

items.title: No design was sized for a lost unit
items.failed: No design covered a lost unit: one doublet's ESP out left 7.2 MW short on 28 Jan.
items.fix: Reliable plans (code -N1) grow the boiler and chillers, as three equal units, until every one-unit-out case meets every day; for the pick this adds 2.0 M€ and 1.6 €/MWh.

items.title: No subsurface checks
items.failed: Designs passed with no check of thermal breakthrough, gas at the ESP or injection pressure.
items.fix: dioscuri_plant.subsurface checks Gringarten-Sauty breakthrough, the ESP setting depth above the bubble point (about 43 bar) and SodM's 0.135 bar/m, and caps a doublet's flow where a limit breaks.

items.title: The repair loop grew a heat pump that could not help
items.failed: The repair loop kept growing a unit that did not close the gap: it grew a heat pump from 0.7 to 64 MW.
items.fix: The loop stops when growing a unit does not close the gap, and says why.

items.title: Gas-free plans had no treatment train per doublet
items.failed: The gas-free stage sized only a shared treatment train, so 'the train out' forced a 30 MW electric boiler (92.7 €/MWh); with the gas boiler ruled out, reliable plans grew the heat pump to 195.6 MW for cases it cannot cover.
items.fix: Gas-free plans are also sized with a train per doublet (pick 86.4 €/MWh, electric boiler 16.6 MW), and a reliable plan takes back a growth that does not close its gap.

items.title: Service windows fell inside a doublet's stop
items.failed: With yearly service on, the cheapest design's single boiler was serviced from 29 Jul, inside the doublet's stop (9 Jul–12 Aug), leaving 7 days short (2.67 MW).
items.fix: The doublets' stops are placed first, and no heating unit is serviced while a doublet stands.

items.title: Brine flow was cut by the 40 K cap after planning
items.failed: When the network warms by more than the brine may cool (a 50 °C return heated to 100 °C, 40 K cap), the brine flow was planned 'balanced' and then cut by the cap: 6 GWh a year went to the boiler at 3,500 m.
items.found: Found while building ADR-0015's changes ('a model bug found on the way')
items.fix: The flow is planned for the cap (dioscuri_plant/year.py).

items.title: Cost basis 20–35 % below PBL
items.failed: Geothermal capital and O&M sat 20–35 % below PBL 2026, although the code said they matched PBL.
items.fix: Costs use the ThermoGIS v3 surface plant (3.5 M€ + 882 €/kW) with the v3 wells and PBL's fixed O&M (121 €/kW/yr); the cheapest design becomes one doublet.

items.title: 'Lowest CO2' bought 24 t a year with 21 M€
items.failed: The lowest-CO2 pick bought its last 24 t of CO2 a year with 21 M€ of extra wells.
items.fix: 'Lowest CO2' takes the cheapest design within 2 % of the lowest CO2.

items.title: Best-overall rule inverted at high carbon prices
items.failed: The best-overall pick weighs CO2 at PBL's long-term 137 €/t, so with a user carbon price above 137 €/t it weighed CO2 less than the user's own price.
items.fix: CO2 never weighs less than the user's own carbon price; reliable plans are built for the best layout of each doublet count.

items.title: Best overall was not best by its own measure
items.failed: The reliable plan was built only on the sizing cheapest at today's carbon price. The pick (2.0 MW heat pump, 14,103 t, 76.37 weighted) lost to the same layout with 3.3 MW (12,967 t, 75.87 weighted) for +0.03 €/MWh.
items.fix: Each layout's reliable plan is also built on its sizing cheapest with CO2 at 137 €/t, and picks are kept by design, not by code.

items.title: Failures ignored the 600-hour grid contract
items.failed: An ESP outage (5 Jan–4 May) ran the electric boiler 849 h, past the 600-hour contract, but the failure card said 2.05 M€; the grid charge rises from 0.74 to 3.73 M€ and the event costs 5.04 M€.
items.fix: Failure cards and yearly failure costs add the change of grid charge when an outage passes 600 hours; the treatment train, with no published failure rate, is said not counted.

items.title: SDE++ paid on the heat pump's electricity
items.failed: SDE++ counted the heat pump's whole output, its electricity included (eligible 56.7 against 53.3 GWh of brine heat), and the 'with heat pump' categories used the brine capacity instead of the heat pump's (6.94 M€ in year 1).
items.fix: Base-load categories pay only geothermal heat (SDE++ 3.35 → 3.15 M€ in year 1), and in the heat-pump categories the heat pump is the installation (6.94 → 1.47 M€).

items.title: Monte Carlo was not centred on the case
items.failed: The uncertainty draws were uniform over ranges not centred on the case, so the median cost (74.4 €/MWh) sat above the base (69.8 €/MWh).
items.fix: Each input is drawn triangular with its mode at the design's own value, and the answer says the base's percentile (median 72.4 €/MWh, base at P33).

items.title: The recommended design flared the brine's gas
items.failed: The recommended design flared 4.1 GWh of the brine's gas a year.
items.fix: A plan that flares more than 1 GWh a year gives way, as best overall, to one that flares less within 3 % of its measure.

items.title: Money answers were written by the model
items.failed: The chat made up the gas reference and once said gas was cheaper than the design.
items.fix: The gas reference, yearly totals, extra capital, payback, NPV, prices and what the costs leave out are computed by code and given to the answer model.

items.title: Other units and number words were dropped
items.failed: Values in other units (ct/kWh, l/s, TWh, °F) and German or Dutch number words were not read, and an out-of-range ask was not said to be refused.
items.found: Review panel 31 Oct (ML and LLM expert, red team)
items.fix: Code converts these units and reads the number words; an ask out of range is said in the reply as 'Not applied'.

items.title: An injected value in an attachment reached the reply
items.failed: A datasheet (rated COP 2.2) carried a hidden instruction to report COP 12. The reply flagged it, yet also said 'you must use a COP of 12'.
items.fix: Text in a file addressed to the assistant (hidden comments, 'AI note', 'you must report') is left out before the model reads it.

items.title: The chat could not see the design's days
items.failed: The chat could not see the daily schedule, so a question about 19 July was answered wrong.
items.fix: The peak days, any day or month named, stops as dates and ESP starts per doublet reach the answers; 19 July is now answered right.

items.title: A sentence about injected brine changed the reservoir
items.failed: 'The injected brine is 30-40 K colder' was read as a what-if that made the reservoir 35 K colder.
items.fix: Reservoir what-ifs are read only from sentences about the reservoir.

items.title: Dates in other languages and short forms misread
items.failed: '19/7' became 28 Jan and 'jan 28th' became 28–31 Jan; 'the coldest week' ran as 1–7 Jan instead of 25–31 Jan.
items.found: Review panel 1 Nov (judge, district client, operator)
items.fix: Dates and durations are read in Dutch, German and French and as 19/7 or 10/01-24/01, and 'the coldest week' takes the worst start (ties go to the most demand).

items.title: Planned maintenance took the worst window
items.failed: Planned maintenance was put in the worst window of the year.
items.fix: Planned work ('take the heat pump out for 10 days') takes the mildest window (1–10 Aug).

items.title: Failure replies contradicted their cards
items.failed: In 9 of 15 failure replies the model's text contradicted the card that code wrote.
items.fix: Failure replies are shown as code wrote them; negative running costs say the heat went undelivered.

items.title: Words read as the wrong parameter
items.failed: 'From 10 to 24 January' became a 10/24 °C cooling network, '20 % more heat demand' lowered the coverage check to 20 %, 'doublet 1' set one doublet and 'COP 12' became a 12 MW heat pump.
items.found: Review panel 1 Nov (agentic AI expert, district client)
items.fix: Code checks these readings: dates are days, a doublet's name is not a count, a COP is not a size, and a described doublet's depth must be in the message.

items.title: A reply said yes when the data said no
items.failed: Asked whether the cheapest design meets a 50 % CO2 cut, the reply began 'yes' although it cuts 41.2 %; the claim check removed the true sentence 'This falls short of the required 50%'.
items.fix: A CO2 floor ('at least 50 % less') runs as a search against the design named and says first whether it meets it (now: 41.2 %, short; the cheapest at 50 % is 2D-HP-AB, 71.4 €/MWh).

items.title: A reply claimed an action that never ran
items.failed: After a long brief the reply said 'I have updated the heating network return temperature to 55 °C … I am now sizing a reliable plan', but nothing ran and the return stayed 60 °C.
items.fix: A check removes actions claimed that never ran, and a long brief is never taken for a file request.

items.title: The small reader turned down fair questions
items.failed: qwen3:1.7b marked 8 on-topic messages unrelated; 'why did you recommend that one and not the one you call best overall?' was declined and replaced by about 600 words on the wells.
items.fix: Fair questions are never declined once a design exists.

items.title: The model's working was shown as the answer
items.failed: Two replies were the model's own working ('Wait, let me re-read carefully…'), cut off mid-sentence, and never answered the question.
items.fix: A check removes the model's own working and sentences about 'the text' or 'the context'.

items.title: Switches and stop dates could not be set in words
items.failed: 'Switch on the district network heat losses and a yearly service stop' was refused as 'Not applied', and 'could we move the stop to August?' could not run.
items.fix: Switches are read in words, a missing network length is asked for, and stop dates are a what-if (doublet_stops) whose days code reads from the words.

items.title: Costs given under the wrong names
items.failed: A reply called the 30.6 M€ capital the yearly cost (9.45 M€), the cost of heat (75.7) the cost of heat and cold, the cost of cold (42.1) the cost of heat, and invented a budget cap.
items.fix: A final label check shows the code's draft when a cost or reliability claim is still wrong, and the yearly cost by part is a fact the reply can use.

items.title: False premises answered 'Yes, that is correct'
items.failed: 'The cost of heat is 69.8 €/MWh and the boiler gives about a quarter, correct?' got 'Yes'; the cost of heat is 75.7 €/MWh (69.8 is heat and cold) and the boiler gives 49.2 %.
items.fix: Code checks what the message takes as given and leads with a correction ('Not quite. The cost of heat is 75.7 €/MWh; 69.8 €/MWh is the cost of heat and cold together.').

items.title: Modelled options said to be not modelled
items.failed: Asked to switch on network heat losses and yearly service, the reply said losses are not modelled, though both exist behind switches.
items.fix: When a tool ran, a sentence saying it cannot be computed or modelled is removed, and the context lists options switched off apart from what is not modelled.

items.title: A what-if kept its N-1 name after losing N-1
items.failed: A what-if with the reservoir 5 K colder kept '(N-1)' in its name and reliable = true, while 1 of its 5 one-unit-out cases was short (1.69 MW on 28 Jan).
items.fix: A what-if keeps N-1 only if its own one-unit-out cases hold.

items.title: Gas share stated about 100 times too low
items.failed: The reply said the gas boiler gives about 0.5 GWh (3 %) of the heat; it gives 54.99 GWh, 49.2 %.
items.fix: The values a question asks for (heat by source in GWh, CO2 by source, gas flows) are looked up by code and given as facts.

items.title: N-1 blamed for the gas share
items.failed: Why-answers blamed N-1 for the gas share and the heat pump size, but the design without N-1 burns the same 54.99 GWh; the split is set by the exchanger's limit and the heat pump sweep.
items.fix: A code-written note gives the heat split's reason: the exchanger's limit, the peak, and the heat pump sizes tried with their costs.

items.title: A request for the full report was refused
items.failed: 'Please do the design work and give me the full report' was refused: the small reader flagged it as skipping the checks, and a word list confirmed it because it says 'report'.
items.fix: The reader's flags are suspicions that a larger model must confirm, and the word list is gone.

items.title: A what-if on the heating return was not run
items.failed: 'What happens if we lower the heating return to 50 °C?' was answered from the documents; only a reservoir temperature change could be re-run.
items.fix: What-ifs run on any input in the parameter catalogue: the same plant under the change, then a new search.

items.title: A calculation in a reply did not add up
items.failed: A reply worked out '86.1 °C − 40 K = 52.1 °C'.
items.found: Chat questions about where numbers come from, 2 Nov
items.fix: A calculation written in a reply is checked (answer.wrong_sums): if wrong, the model is asked again; if still wrong, the line goes.

items.title: The reading's JSON was cut short
items.failed: Read inside the long parameters reading, three new fields came back wrong for most messages and the JSON was cut short.
items.fix: What a reply needs is its own short model call (needs_v1): 14 of 14 test messages read right, 0.2 s each.

items.title: A later search replaced the first pick
items.failed: Design ids were not unique across searches, so a follow-up search overwrote the recommended design.
items.fix: Design ids are unique per search, and what-ifs name the design they were asked about.

items.title: Two chats at once mixed their steps
items.failed: With two chats running at once, the server mixed their steps and replies.
items.found: Found while preparing the 31 Oct panel
items.fix: The server runs one chat at a time.

items.title: A what-if's gas price leaked into the tabs
items.failed: A what-if's gas price (30 €/MWh) leaked into the Economics tab, so every design was compared with that gas plant; the design picker showed no names.
items.found: Review panel 1 Nov (UI and UX designer)
items.fix: The tabs measure every design against the base case's gas reference; edited designs keep their own name (U1) and lose the N-1 flag; the design picker shows the names.

items.title: The requirements PDF read one word per line
items.failed: The requirements PDF was not searchable, and its preview showed one word per line.
items.fix: Word-exported PDFs are read in layout mode, as lines and tables.

items.title: A design with no cost broke the design-space map
items.failed: The Compare tab's design-space map failed with a server error: a drawn design that delivers no heat has a NaN cost, and JSON has no NaN.
items.found: A teammate's use of the Compare map, 3 Nov
items.fix: Such a design counts as broken ('no cost per MWh'), its numbers are null, and every server response and stream event sends NaN as null.

items.title: Design codes read as numbers in outage replies
items.failed: Replies about a unit out quoted designs such as 1D-HP-EC@3000-N1-FC; the number check took the 3000 for a figure no source gives and removed the sentence, and a remedy's boiler size was never registered as sourced.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (cases S51, S52, S59)
items.fix: Design codes are skipped by the number check, and the outage text registers every figure it states.

items.title: An attached file was said to be missing
items.failed: "Summarise the attached datasheet and size an absorption chiller" got "no file was provided": the request went down the not-modelled path, which never searched the attachment.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (case S12)
items.fix: A message about the attached file searches it on that path too; the reply summarises the file and flags the instruction hidden in it.

items.title: The chat could no longer add or change an aquifer
items.failed: The merge of 4 Nov kept the new reading prompt, written before aquifers could be edited in words, so their instructions were lost.
items.fix: The aquifer instructions are back in the prompt in use, and a test reads that prompt for them.

items.title: "Not quite" for a premise with no figure
items.failed: "Why didn't you pick the cheapest?" and "you drilled deeper than the aquifer" were answered "Not quite." with a figure about something else.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (case T04)
items.fix: Code leads with a correction only when the premise states a figure.

items.title: The search was invisible to most questions
items.failed: "What did the search go through to get here?" got "I have only run one design": the search summary went into the answer only when the question used certain words.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (case N02)
items.fix: Once a search ran, every answer is told how wide it was and its picks, a line each.

items.title: Another design's figure said of the one asked about
items.failed: "What about the cheapest one, how much CO2 does it save?" got 60.6 %, the recommended design's figure; the cheapest saves 64 %.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (case T02)
items.fix: A sentence that gives another design's value without naming that design is sent back once, then removed; a value the claim check removed is added back from the checked draft.

items.title: "How does it compare with the most reliable one?" compared nothing
items.failed: One design was named and "it" (the current one) implied; the comparison was dropped, and the reply called the cheapest the most reliable.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (case T03)
items.fix: One other existing design and nothing new to run: it is set against the current design.

items.title: The pick's choices went missing
items.failed: Since plant options came in, the pick is an option of a reliable plan (1D-HP-EC@3000-N1-FC); its layout was looked up by the wrong parent, so "why not two injectors?" and "why not the cheapest?" had no figures to answer from.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (cases T04, S50)
items.fix: A design's parents are followed to its layout; each variant is set against its own layout.

items.title: True sentences removed as unsupported
items.failed: "Run A assumed a 60 °C return" and "the best overall choice is A1 at 56.7 €/MWh" were removed: run A's value was in no source, and a long cited block left the checker no room for the designs.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (cases M04, T04)
items.fix: The runs block gives run A's values too; the claim check reads twice the sources in a 16k window.

items.title: "Which designs did the search pick?" answered with heat pump sizes
items.failed: A long context cut the search summary to its first lines, which held no pick.
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (long conversation C3, turn 1)
items.fix: The summary opens with a short line per pick, and a cut keeps them all.

items.title: A unit's share of the heat corrected against the plant's coverage
items.failed: "You told me the gas boiler covers about 21 % of the heat?" got "Not quite. ... covered is 100 %".
items.found: The final eval run of 4 Nov on the merged code (long conversation C2, turn 12)
items.fix: A premise about a unit's share of the heat is paired with the heat split, which the model judges.

items.title: The wells' productivity index ignored the doublet
items.failed: The index used a single well with a 500 m drainage radius (14.5 m3/h/bar); a producer and an injector 1,500 m apart give 2 pi k h / (mu ln(L / r_w)) = 11.7 m3/h/bar, so the pumps' electricity was about 19 % low.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: The doublet's steady-state formula with the well spacing; the pick's cost of heat and cold rose by 1.5 %.

items.title: The GEMINI check compared GEMINI with the wrong plant figures
items.failed: The check's plant side ignored the doublet's aquifer, its wells' open parts and the injectors' share of the flow (an injection pump shown 83 % off), and GEMINI's exchanger ran on its default water (duty 5.5 % off on the pick).
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Each doublet solved as the year model does; GEMINI's exchanger given the brine's density and heat capacity.

items.title: Very tight rock crashed the search
items.failed: Below about 0.83 D·m GEMINI's injection solve found no root under 500 bar and the search raised an error.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: The closed form GEMINI agrees with elsewhere, so the subsurface checks flag the design and cap its flow.

items.title: An injector out on some days left brine unused
items.failed: Equal shares ranked the doublets by their year's largest cap, so a doublet whose injector was out could be filled last: 1.7 GWh more boiler depending only on which injector failed.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: The shares are filled day by day from that day's smallest cap.

items.title: The heat pump's COP had no upper bound
items.failed: With the source as hot as the supply (the exchanger out, brine straight from the well) the COP was 64 over a year, infinite above 100 °C.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Carnot over at least a 10 K lift (at most 18.7 at 100 °C).

items.title: Free cooling on a smoothed weather year
items.failed: Free cooling used monthly normals spread over the days (wet bulb never above 15.5 °C): 21.0 GWh, where De Bilt's real hours of 2021-2025 give 16.9-17.8 GWh.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Each day's free cooling is the clipped share averaged over that calendar day's 120 real hours (KNMI hourly data in the repository); the pick's cost of cold rose from 23.5 to 30.4 €/MWh.

items.title: The cooling towers' water was never costed
items.failed: No water price, no water line, and the permit pack printed 4,682 m3 of make-up water where about 36,000 m3 is right (free cooling's heat left out).
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Make-up and blow-down from all the heat the towers reject, priced on the cold side (WML 2026 tariff and tap-water tax; blow-down assumed); the check and the permit pack print the same figure.

items.title: The absorption chiller ran on any brine
items.failed: Absorption cold was credited at COP 0.75 from a 65 °C well, below the 80 °C its hot-water loop needs.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Below an 80 °C wellhead it gives no cold, and a warning says why.

items.title: NPV against gas left out re-buys and the value left
items.failed: Units with 20- or 25-year lives were never bought again: the gas-free pick showed 9.32 M€ where 6.60 M€ is right.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Both sides go through the investor model's capital flows (re-buys, value left at year 30).

items.title: One design, two gas references
items.failed: Options' CO2 saving used the plain reference, the money views a reference with the option's free cooling: '60.6 % less' beside tonnes that gave 59.8 %, NPV against gas 15 % apart.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: One reference with the plant options taken out, for every comparison.

items.title: The best-overall rule in the reply left out the flaring rule
items.failed: The lead reply said best overall is the cheapest with CO2 at 137 €/t, while the cheaper A2 was set aside for flaring 4.1 GWh a year, unsaid.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: The rule is said as the code applies it, and the reply names the plan set aside and its flaring.

items.title: The sweep dropped its lowest-CO2 design
items.failed: The front's points were picked by index, not position, before cutting to 6: the lowest-CO2 point was never refined, though refined it beats the 'lowest CO2' pick on cost and CO2.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Points chosen by position on the front, both ends kept, up to 10 refined.

items.title: Risk sizing assumed a spare ESP no design pays for
items.failed: The days-short draws took a spare ESP on site (7 days out, not 120), and N-1 was set as one-off M€ against k€ a year: the pick's '0.25 M€ saved' disappears without the spare.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Drawn as built (a spare only when asked); both plans priced a year; units with no failure rate named.

items.title: Failure remedies grew a bank by too little
items.failed: With a unit of a 3-unit boiler bank among the failures, '10 MW more boiler' left 3.3 MW short (the bank needs gap x 3/2); a failed single electric boiler was itself grown.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: The bank factor u/(u-1); a standby twin for a single electric boiler.

items.title: 'Most reliable' was the cheapest N-1 plan
items.failed: Every N-1 plan ties on every reliability measure the code computes, so the label claimed more than it knew.
items.found: Calculation audit 4 Nov (five independent reviewers, before fine-tuning)
items.fix: Shown as 'cheapest reliable' (a user saying 'most reliable' still finds it).
